Explain the example for scan keys in small batches

blocks.text: SCAN walks through key names using a cursor. It is safer for large keyspaces than asking for every matching key in one blocking command.
Use a local Redis server and redis-cli. Commands here use cma: practice keys only. Redis commands do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Do not connect these exercises to a production database.
Read the code step by step

items: `SCAN` returns a continuation cursor. Keep iterating until the returned cursor is zero.
`MATCH` finds the described graph pattern. Labels and arrow direction narrow the connections being followed.

blocks.text: The response includes a next cursor and some matching keys. Continue with that cursor until it returns 0.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: COUNT is a hint, not an exact batch size. A changing keyspace can produce duplicates, so callers must account for that.
